question.problem:
Consider the following partitions:

- ${P}_{1}=\{{x}_{0},{x}_{1},…,{x}_{m}\}$ is a partition of the interval $[1,2]$

- ${P}_{2}=\{{y}_{0},{y}_{1},…,{y}_{n}\}$ is a partition of the interval $[1,2]$

Calculate ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}2Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j},$ where $Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i}-{x}_{i-1}$ and $Δ{y}_{j}={y}_{j}-{y}_{j-1}.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the constant multiple and product rules, we can write the summation as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}2Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} & =2{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{x}_{i}Δ{y}_{j} \\  & =2{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that both ${\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}$ and ${\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}$ are equal to the length of the interval $[1,2].$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i} & =2-1=1, \\ {\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j} & =2-1=1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Combining our results, we have 

$$
2{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}Δ{x}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}Δ{y}_{j}=2\cdot 1\cdot 1=2.
$$
